summaries.plain:
Invoice PDF pagination work is substantially resolved. Added `_row_height()` to consistently convert points to page-height units, and refactored continuation-table header reservation so it is calculated once per document. This changed the usable page budget from `page_height - 54` to `page_height - 36` while preserving headers on continuation pages. A new regression test for an 86-line invoice now expects two pages and passes. The invoice PDF suite passes (`14 passed, 1 skipped`), the broader billing suite passes (`83 passed, 4 skipped`), and existing golden PDFs remain byte-stable. The remaining recommended validation is visual inspection of the three generated PDFs.

The broader test baseline is healthy: `148 passed, 2 skipped`, with six deprecation warnings.

A separate SQLAlchemy 2.0 cleanup has started. Legacy session factories were located in `ledgerly/db.py`, `ledgerly/repositories.py`, and `tests/conftest.py`; `make_engine()` still passes the removed `echo=True` option. `ledgerly/models.py` has been migrated from `declarative_base()` to `DeclarativeBase` with a `Base` subclass. Repository code still contains two deprecated `Invoice.query.get(invoice_id)` calls, alongside valid `session.get()` usages; these query calls remain to be migrated. No post-migration test run has yet been reported.

Keep the operator’s priority on settlement reconciliation for unmatched processor transactions and ledger entries. Do not resume the account-deletion safeguard unless requested. Privacy approval is no longer needed; reviewer is @dmitri. Other backlog items are the potentially incomplete Go rename, BigQuery retention restriction, EXPLAIN ANALYZE gate, credit-note/refund review, and Go tag publication. Deployment channel: `#deploy-cobalt`.
